# 1 Kings Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-Ben-hadad king-of Aram gathered all his-army, and-thirty-two kings were with-him, and-horses and-chariots. And-he-went-up and-besieged Samaria and-fought against-it.

**2** And-he-sent messengers to-Ahab king-of Israel, to-the-city, and-said to-him, "Thus says Ben-hadad:

**3** 'Your-silver and-your-gold — mine they-are; and-your-wives and-your-sons, the-best — mine they-are.'"

**4** And-the-king-of Israel answered and-said, "According-to-your-word, my-lord the-king — I am yours and-all that-I-have."

**5** And-the-messengers returned and-said, "Thus says Ben-hadad, saying, 'I sent to-you, saying, "Your-silver and-your-gold and-your-wives and-your-sons you-shall-give to-me."

**6** But at-this time tomorrow I-will-send my-servants to-you, and-they-will-search your-house and-the-houses-of your-servants, and-all that-is-precious in-your-eyes they-will-put in-their-hand and-take.'"

**7** And-the-king-of Israel called all the-elders-of the-land and-said, "Know, please, and-see that this-one is-seeking evil, for he-sent to-me for-my-wives and-for-my-sons and-for-my-silver and-for-my-gold, and-I-did-not refuse-him."

**8** And-all the-elders and-all the-people said to-him, "Do-not listen, and-do-not consent."

**9** And-he-said to-the-messengers-of Ben-hadad, "Say to-my-lord the-king, 'All that you-sent for-your-servant at-the-first I-will-do, but-this thing I-am-not able to-do.'" And-the-messengers went and-brought-him-back word.

**10** And-Ben-hadad sent to-him and-said, "Thus may-the-gods do to-me and-more, if the-dust-of Samaria suffices for-handfuls for-all the-people who are at-my-feet."

**11** And-the-king-of Israel answered and-said, "Tell-him, 'Let-not the-one-who-girds boast like-the-one-who-looses.'"

**12** And-it-was when-he-heard this word — and-he was drinking, he and-the-kings, in-the-booths — and-he-said to-his-servants, "Set-yourselves." And-they-set-themselves against the-city.

**13** And-behold — one prophet drew-near to-Ahab king-of Israel and-said, "Thus says YHWH: 'Have-you-seen all this great multitude? Behold, I am-giving-it into-your-hand today, and-you-will-know that I am YHWH.'"

**14** And-Ahab said, "By-whom?" And-he-said, "Thus says YHWH: 'By-the-young-men-of the-commanders-of the-provinces.'" And-he-said, "Who shall-begin the-battle?" And-he-said, "You."

**15** And-he-mustered ʾet-the-young-men-of the-commanders-of the-provinces, and-they-were two-hundred and-thirty-two. And-after-them he-mustered all the-people, all the-sons-of Israel — seven thousand.

**16** And-they-went-out at-noon. And-Ben-hadad was drinking-himself-drunk in-the-booths — he and-the-kings, the-thirty-two kings helping-him.

**17** And-the-young-men-of the-commanders-of the-provinces went-out first. And-Ben-hadad sent, and-they-told-him, saying, "Men have-come-out from-Samaria."

**18** And-he-said, "Whether for-peace they-come-out, seize-them alive; and-whether for-war they-come-out, alive seize-them."

**19** And-these went-out from-the-city — the-young-men-of the-commanders-of the-provinces — and-the-army that was after-them.

**20** And-each-one struck his-man, and-Aram fled, and-Israel pursued-them. And-Ben-hadad king-of Aram escaped on-a-horse with-horsemen.

**21** And-the-king-of Israel went-out and-struck the-horses and-the-chariots, and-struck Aram with-a-great striking.

**22** And-the-prophet drew-near to the-king-of Israel and-said to-him, "Go, strengthen-yourself, and-know and-see what you-will-do, for at-the-turn-of the-year the-king-of Aram is-coming-up against-you."

**23** And-the-servants-of the-king-of Aram said to-him, "A-god-of mountains is their-god; therefore they-were-stronger than-us. But let-us-fight-them in-the-plain — surely we-will-be-stronger than-them.

**24** And-this thing do: remove the-kings, each-one from-his-place, and-put governors in-their-place.

**25** And-you, number for-yourself an-army like the-army that fell from-you, and-horse like-horse and-chariot like-chariot. And-we-will-fight-them in-the-plain — surely we-will-be-stronger than-them." And-he-listened to-their-voice and-did so.

**26** And-it-was at-the-turn-of the-year, and-Ben-hadad mustered Aram and-went-up to-Aphek, to-the-battle with-Israel.

**27** And-the-sons-of Israel were-mustered and-were-provisioned and-went to-meet-them. And-the-sons-of Israel encamped before-them like-two-little-flocks-of goats, and-Aram filled ʾet-the-land.

**28** And-the-man-of God drew-near and-said to the-king-of Israel, and-said, "Thus says YHWH: 'Because Aram has-said, "A-god-of mountains is YHWH, and-he-is-not a-god-of valleys," I-will-give ʾet-all this great multitude into-your-hand, and-you-will-know that I am YHWH.'"

**29** And-they-encamped these opposite those seven days. And-it-was on-the-seventh day, and-the-battle drew-near. And-the-sons-of Israel struck Aram — a-hundred thousand foot-soldiers in-one day.

**30** And-the-rest fled to-Aphek, into the-city. And-the-wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men who-were-left. And-Ben-hadad fled and-came into-the-city, into-an-inner-chamber.

**31** And-his-servants said to-him, "Behold, please, we-have-heard that the-kings-of the-house-of Israel — that they are kings-of ḥesed. Let-us-put, please, sackcloth on-our-loins and-ropes on-our-heads, and-go-out to the-king-of Israel. Perhaps he-will-spare your-life."

**32** And-they-girded sackcloth on-their-loins and-ropes on-their-heads, and-came to the-king-of Israel and-said, "Your-servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please, let-my-life live.'" And-he-said, "Is-he still alive? He is my-brother."

**33** And-the-men divined and-quickly caught-it, and-they-said, "Your-brother Ben-hadad!" And-he-said, "Go, bring-him." And-Ben-hadad came-out to-him, and-he-brought-him-up into-the-chariot.

**34** And-he-said to-him, "The-cities that my-father took from-your-father I-will-return, and-streets you-shall-make for-yourself in-Damascus, as my-father made in-Samaria." "And-I — with-a-covenant I-will-send-you-away." And-he-cut a-covenant with-him and-sent-him-away.

**35** And-a-certain man from-the-sons-of the-prophets said to-his-companion by-the-word-of YHWH, "Strike-me, please." And-the-man refused to-strike-him.

**36** And-he-said to-him, "Because you-did-not listen to-the-voice-of YHWH, behold — you are-going from-me, and-the-lion will-strike-you." And-he-went from-beside-him, and-the-lion found-him and-struck-him.

**37** And-he-found another man and-said, "Strike-me, please." And-the-man struck-him, striking and-wounding.

**38** And-the-prophet went and-stood-before the-king on-the-road, and-disguised-himself with-a-bandage over his-eyes.

**39** And-it-was as-the-king passed-by, and-he cried to the-king and-said, "Your-servant went-out into-the-midst-of the-battle, and-behold — a-man turned-aside and-brought to-me a-man and-said, 'Guard this man. If he-is-surely missing, your-life shall-be for-his-life, or a-talent-of silver you-shall-weigh-out.'

**40** And-it-was — your-servant was-doing here and-there — and-he was-gone." And-the-king-of Israel said to-him, "So is your-judgment; you yourself have-decided."

**41** And-he-hurried and-removed ʾet-the-bandage from-upon his-eyes, and-the-king-of Israel recognized-him, that he was from-the-prophets.

**42** And-he-said to-him, "Thus says YHWH: 'Because you-sent-away the-man-of my-destruction from-your-hand, your-life shall-be for-his-life, and-your-people for-his-people.'"

**43** And-the-king-of Israel went to his-house sullen and-angry, and-came to-Samaria.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **20:11 — "Let-not the-one-who-girds boast"**: Ahab's proverb: don't boast when putting on armor — boast when taking it off. A rare moment of wit from Israel's most condemned king.
2. **20:23 — "a-god-of mountains"**: Aram's theological error: they assume YHWH's power is geographically limited. God's response in v. 28 directly refutes this — YHWH is God of valleys too.
3. **20:31 — "kings-of ḥesed"**: Aram's servants have heard that Israel's kings show mercy. This reputation — perhaps undeserved by Ahab — saves Ben-hadad's life, but at a cost.
4. **20:42 — "the-man-of my-destruction"**: Hebrew ʾish ḥermi — "the man of my ban/devotion to destruction." Ben-hadad was under divine ḥerem; Ahab's release of him was a covenantal violation.

— EMET
